<span id="paper-foundation-models-adaloop-vision-ed1ee6f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5b64a38a09f4bf8">Should visual AdaLoop use identical modulation for different questions about the same image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The pooled question vector conditions the visual block on the evidence each question needs. Loops add processing opportunities, not a guarantee of locating details. Shared images do not imply identical visual processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting cups and reading text on them can produce different modulation vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5b64a38a09f4bf8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-403999afca57c3bc">Why can repeated vision loops change representations when encoder weights are frozen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen parameters do not freeze hidden state. Each loop feeds updated state into a shared block modulated by the question vector. Deep supervision trains different depths, and deployment stopping must compare predictions without reading gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question about objects and another about occlusion can direct the same encoder toward different details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403999afca57c3bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-15a64e71d1ec71fe">How do vision loops differ from adding language-model reasoning tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra language steps operate in the text stream. AdaLoop spends compute on question-conditioned visual encoding with shared weights and updated visual state. Compare matched training and budgets before claiming superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting occluded objects can revisit vision features instead of only extending text reasoning after a single encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15a64e71d1ec71fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-acf4971fdf9cd572">Can stable-answer stopping inspect the gold label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deployment checks whether successive predictions agree. Training supervises several depths with positive weights summing to one. The local C interface also requires externally supplied detached draft embeddings and a fixed separator; it does not generate drafts itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two consecutive predictions of “three” can trigger stopping even when the true answer is “four.”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acf4971fdf9cd572">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-frames-on-demand-ec1c6746" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f9ed6ab63e2f74a">Does caption-once mean writing a new video caption for each question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Build one reusable text memory, then route and budget additional vision separately for each question. Count initial captioning and per-query frame access separately; memory reuse does not mean all queries avoid visual compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five questions can share one caption, and only the question needing additional detail may require frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f9ed6ab63e2f74a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5d97e558e97b297">Why add a visual-need router after building caption memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text remembers broad events but may omit details needed later. The router decides whether text evidence suffices and spends more vision budget only when needed. This controls evidence-acquisition cost; captions are not lossless and a routing decision is not an answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“Someone picks up a box” can answer whether an object was taken, but reading its serial number may require looking at frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5d97e558e97b297">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78351d40c96d69a6">What is the trade-off versus uniformly resampling the video for every question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform sampling repeatedly pays vision cost. On-demand access reuses a caption and focuses on uncertain frames, but a missed detail or routing error can hide key evidence. Compare real quality on identical questions and budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten event-order queries may share memory; a brief action in the last query still needs the right frame.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78351d40c96d69a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d826d052ddc75b2">Do three-seed local caption/query gates validate the learned visual-need router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reference state transitions check gating, top-K frame selection, and budget; there is no long-video VLM or trained semantic router. This does not prove the system can tell which questions text answers or reproduce frame savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rule can select at most three frames without knowing whether any contains the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d826d052ddc75b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hawk" data-paper-title="HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-hawk-938adaa0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-969c6e9709068ac4">What are the target and drafter roles in HAWK speculative decoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahawk">HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cheaper drafter proposes tokens; the target verifies them and preserves the output distribution. HAWK compresses multiple target layers for a shallow drafter to improve proposals, not to bypass verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shallow model proposes several words, then the larger model checks how many can be accepted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00623">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00623-hawk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-969c6e9709068ac4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hawk" data-paper-title="HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6e2431346cfbada">Why train the HAWK drafter on shifted trajectories after its own proposals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahawk">HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposed tokens put the system on drafter-generated prefixes. Training only on teacher prefixes hides that shift. Shifted trajectories align supervision with actual proposal states, and a mix of teacher layers conveys visual information. The target must still verify acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the first draft token chooses different wording, the second should learn the target distribution under that actual prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00623">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00623-hawk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6e2431346cfbada">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hawk" data-paper-title="HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-08951b88c5bc06ae">How does HAWK&#x27;s learned layer mix differ from using only the final target layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahawk">HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Softmax-normalized trainable weights combine hidden states from multiple layers; final-only is a fixed choice of one source. Weights sum to one but need not be equal. Mixing alone proves neither acceptance-rate gains nor speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high layer weight increases its share in the mixed representation rather than concatenating layers as extra tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00623">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00623-hawk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08951b88c5bc06ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hawk" data-paper-title="HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e1157c08ff9a8f8">Does local HAWK validation include a specialized decoding kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahawk">HAWK: Rethinking Multimodal Drafting for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks softmax-weighted target hidden states, shifted-target supervision, and target isolation. It does not run a complete speculative verification loop or specialized kernel, so cannot demonstrate end-to-end lossless speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Checking that three weights sum to one does not measure accepted tokens or saved generation time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00623">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.00623-hawk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e1157c08ff9a8f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-muse-glimmer-30b-d492f01f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c695941cc5721c5a">Why count weights, KV, vision, and drafter memory together for Muse Glimmer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Device memory must hold the entire inference process. Long agent context grows KV, and vision and speculative heads add memory. A quantized language model under a size cap does not alone fit a 32GB device. Use real inputs and deployment settings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weights below 20 GB may still leave too little space for long-trajectory KV and temporary vision tensors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与结构. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c695941cc5721c5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e53a66d94151563">Why is three local layers followed by one global layer different from shortening every context window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local layers limit most interactions, while global layers still exchange distant information. GQA separately reduces KV heads. These are architectural trade-offs, not reproduction of distillation, post-training, or device performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A distant heading can affect the current paragraph in a global layer, while local layers process adjacent sentences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与结构. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e53a66d94151563">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-228de77c3730310a">How does late-stage cross-entropy differ from fitting truncated teacher logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distillation uses teacher predictions, but top-k truncation drops the tail. Late cross-entropy directly supervises the target token; the paper connects the switch to truncation bias. It is not correct to describe the entire recipe as teacher matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>CE still uses a target token even if the saved teacher top-k omitted it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-228de77c3730310a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-79ddf2ee2885b4c8">Can the 52 layers share one attention and RoPE template?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Repeat [Local, Local, Local, Global] 13 times with 32 query heads and two KV heads. Only local layers apply RoPE. The vision branch separately compresses 1024 patches to 256 tokens via 2×2 grouping. One layer is not the 29.6B model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Applying RoPE everywhere or alternating local and global changes the architecture even with 52 layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与结构, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79ddf2ee2885b4c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mwop-c24139ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b6ef536b9d9ff84">Why can one MWOP attention head have different modality-path importance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One head can support vision→vision, text→vision, and text→text interactions with unequal contributions. MWOP assesses and prunes paths within a head rather than treating it as indivisible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep text reading vision in a head that contributes little to vision-only interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b6ef536b9d9ff84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e71e27b14980f452">Why re-estimate FFN channel importance after pruning attention paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pruning changes FFN input distributions, making old rankings stale. MWOP treats paths such as vision→vision and text→vision separately and prunes FFN channels by modality. Measure quality and actual speed independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing text-to-vision paths can change how much fusion channels contribute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e71e27b14980f452">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c9fc2d7d0b259f3">What changes with modality-specific FFN pruning instead of one common channel mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text and vision tokens can retain different channel sets and capacities. One mask may hide different channel contributions. Sparse masking needs execution support; it does not guarantee hardware speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text-related channels and texture channels may not overlap. Separate masks preserve both kinds, but the kernel must actually skip work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c9fc2d7d0b259f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-82b1ce006c57fdb6">Why not rank MWOP pruning by |w| rather than |w·∂L/∂w|?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The product captures magnitude and current loss sensitivity. Magnitude alone omits sensitivity; absolute value prevents signed contributions from canceling. This local estimate depends on calibration data and path, not a guarantee deletion is harmless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two equal weights with different gradients rank differently under the product but tie by magnitude.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82b1ce006c57fdb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-omnikvquant-a8e321c1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9bc9fa701552ac3">Does OmniKVQuant compress weights or the current context&#x27;s KV cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It targets key/value states stored during inference, not fixed network parameters. Cache grows with context and contains different modality representations; quantized weights do not remove it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same model has identical weights for short text and long audiovisual context, but different KV storage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9bc9fa701552ac3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-936078904d8b48d2">Why not share one global quantization range and rotation across multimodal KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keys may drift over time so a global range loses local precision. Value geometry also differs by modality. Short-window ranges handle temporal shifts and modality-specific rotations handle value geometry; one static rule need not control both errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small audio keys can lose precision when later video keys set the global range; value structure still needs separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-936078904d8b48d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1f98617e99f9653">How does modality-specific rotation differ from using one matrix for all values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared rotation assumes one coordinate transform suits all modalities. Separate rotations allow distinct coordinate systems for audio, vision, and text. Accuracy still depends on calibration and actual distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Image and audio values may have different high-variance directions; one rotation might suit only one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1f98617e99f9653">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cd2907c3a53ebaf">Does the local 2-bit NumPy reference demonstrate a faster GPU KV kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks window quantization and modality-specific transforms. Actual Triton or other kernels need real A100/A30 validation. Packing, unpacking, memory traffic, and fusion affect latency beyond bit width.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Theoretically two-bit values stored and decoded in floating arrays do not yet deliver real two-bit VRAM or bandwidth savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cd2907c3a53ebaf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pace-vlm" data-paper-title="PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pace-vlm-f64143ef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-73728e1c45489aa8">Why can&#x27;t PACE infer equal vision budgets from equal image sizes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apace-vlm">PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal-sized images can differ in global semantic density and local detail. APC estimates both off-diagonal feature similarities and top-K details that differ from background. Pixel count is not a substitute, and budget signals do not guarantee correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A blank wall and a densely printed page at the same resolution need not preserve the same amount of detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27206">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73728e1c45489aa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pace-vlm" data-paper-title="PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0da1b5df32b59d4e">Why separate image scaling and question-dependent token extraction in PACE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apace-vlm">PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scaling controls input encoding cost; extraction controls what continues downstream. Late token dropping cannot reclaim prior encoding. A shallow preview estimates difficulty, and extraction mixes language and visual attention by confidence rather than using one fixed rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shrink a blank image more than a dense menu, then use the question to select relevant regions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27206">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0da1b5df32b59d4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pace-vlm" data-paper-title="PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b6eb0d63a176892">How does DDAE differ from an equal-weight attention average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apace-vlm">PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It converts the dispersions of two normalized attention maps into confidence weights using temperature softmax. Weights can favor different streams depending on evidence. Dispersion is a method signal, not a calibrated probability of correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Concentrated language attention and diffuse vision attention may favor language; another question can reverse the weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27206">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b6eb0d63a176892">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pace-vlm" data-paper-title="PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-79280489155e740b">Does the real-checkpoint run fully validate DDAE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apace-vlm">PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The small real-checkpoint smoke mainly exercises APC. DDAE is checked with equations and unit tests, without the original model fork or kernels. APC excludes diagonal self-similarity and picks the top-K deviations from the local mean. Correct compression direction does not establish lossless quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five correct out of eight before and after compression is a small-sample observation, not verification of DDAE in generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27206">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.27206-pace-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79280489155e740b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rr-vlm-3b3af466" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e52481933a1636d3">What do prelude, recurrent core, and coda do in RR-VLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prelude computes context h. The core combines h with the previous state and updates s repeatedly. The coda reads the final state. They are stages, not independent voting models. Do not overwrite fixed context as though it were recurrent state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Build h once, update s₁ then s₂, and let the coda read s₂.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e52481933a1636d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-beec2c2a8e3eaa21">Why can a recurrent block save stored layers without reducing executed depth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repetition stores one set of weights but pays for every application. Pruning can damage language and the visual interface, so restore text, align the projector, then restore instruction behavior. Stored parameters and inference steps are different axes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five core layers repeated three times execute 15 layers&#x27; worth of work while storing five sets of weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-beec2c2a8e3eaa21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad08559b372ace80">Why align the projector separately during staged recovery after pruning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Surgery can disrupt both language and vision–language alignment. Recover text first, align only the projector next, then restore instructions. The projector stage excludes KD, unlike the two surrounding recovery phases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restore text continuation before adapting image features to avoid confounding language damage and projector mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad08559b372ace80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-85813119e6b229df">What is the local status of frozen teacher and inter-loop KV sharing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher is a separate, intact frozen copy with detached outputs; the student updates only stage-allowed parameters. Local checks verify shared calls and manual unrolling, not incremental decoding with inter-loop KV reuse or throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three calls to the same core confirm parameter sharing, not that all three share one KV cache correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85813119e6b229df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sink-sparse-7f23b46b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-89e77ff6c5528806">Is the static sink mask selected online from a new prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Independent dense calibration aggregates exact block mass, then takes the shortest row prefix satisfying the mass threshold. New inputs reuse the mask. This saves selection cost but depends on cross-prompt and cross-seed stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed calibration may select two regions. A new prompt&#x27;s high-scoring third region does not silently redefine the mask.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89e77ff6c5528806">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa3282e27f8322fe">Why does Sink-Sparse&#x27;s global branch pool sink blocks as well?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It supplies low-resolution context over every token; the sparse branch computes fine selected interactions. They combine via their normalizers, not by adding only missing blocks. Excluding sink changes the compensation distribution, and test examples cannot reselect the offline support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The sparse branch reads the center closely while the global branch still summarizes the whole image, center included.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa3282e27f8322fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d518dd72ce9680f3">Does a full-support sparse mask alone recover dense attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. The output still mixes a pooled global compensation branch, whose distribution may differ. Full support with gap 1 can reduce both branches to the same dense computation and is a sufficient degeneration test. General fusion is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the sparse branch sees every token but the global branch averages multiple tokens per block, their mixture can differ from dense alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d518dd72ce9680f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-366fd7b1d91c36e5">Can block mass be calibrated by averaging Q/K before softmax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Compute dense token probabilities first, average over query blocks, and sum key blocks to preserve unit row mass. Softmax is nonlinear. Local Python gathers establish correctness, not speed from mask sparsity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two queries can attend opposite ends while their mean attends the center. Early averaging loses the true mass at both ends.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本判断与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-366fd7b1d91c36e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-softcache-596bc18d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd266037ebd633fe">Why study which diffusion forwards to skip rather than only shrink the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling calls the same network repeatedly; nearby states may share computation, but unconditional skipping can compound error. SoftCache adapts reuse and progress using change signals while retaining the model. Cache reliability is not a quality metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse when nearby denoising states change little and recompute when they move quickly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd266037ebd633fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d790da7252145cc">Why is SoftCache&#x27;s step-size control more than refresh versus reuse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Standard caches choose whether to recompute on a fixed schedule. SoftCache uses remaining staleness headroom to adjust the step and rebuild the remaining grid, so skipped nodes are not revisited. Extrapolation needs fresh anchors and early or fast-changing regions restrict jumps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skip two of ten planned denoising nodes only if reliable, then reschedule so the same nodes are not computed later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d790da7252145cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-170562c8fa83951d">How do relative probe changes and residual extrapolation serve different purposes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulated changes estimate staleness headroom and decide refresh/step size. Two fresh residuals estimate a trend for the reused value. They are scheduling versus approximation signals and not interchangeable. One anchor cannot define a slope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The probe can say change is small without giving the current residual; the recent actual residuals estimate it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-170562c8fa83951d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-809bbd8b8fe862a3">Can two-point extrapolation run with one fresh residual anchor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No; one anchor gives a constant, and two anchors must be at distinct times. For t&lt;0.1 or probe change above 0.18, do not jump. Clip step size to the endpoint and use a separate cache for each sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first residual has no prior timestamp to form a slope; dividing by a nonexistent time difference is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-809bbd8b8fe862a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-stacktok-c22648c2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f465fb879831c02">Why not keep only the most obviously relevant StackTok positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some questions need several objects or a relationship. A single hotspot can consume the budget and omit necessary evidence. Coverage is not uniform sampling or unconditional diversity; the selected set should serve the question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To compare two car positions, several patches of the most prominent car are insufficient without the other car.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f465fb879831c02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-146cde1710f5ee82">Why can the highest-relevance tokens be a poor fixed-budget subset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They may repeat the same region and omit scene structure. StackTok prioritizes relevance but switches criteria when a budget-dependent coverage reference indicates missing support. Coverage is not a fixed decoration; it depends on question and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many face patches do not supply the doorway location needed for a layout question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-146cde1710f5ee82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47fcf43099b85610">How does adaptive coverage differ from a fixed mixture of two rankings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed mixing holds one relevance/coverage ratio. StackTok switches criteria when current support is insufficient for the budget. This is a selection-time constraint, not a static diversity score; real fixed-budget VLM evaluation remains necessary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With two slots left and missing key regions, fill coverage; once support is sufficient, favor relevance.</p>
