<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47fcf43099b85610">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eccf1fd02dc72752">Does passing the local single-crop selector show acceleration in five VLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It exercises reference-gated selection on one crop, with three-seed fixtures checking ordering, gates, and budgets. No paper VLM is loaded. Correct indices do not establish a shorter forward, latency, or accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten valid distinct indices meet the selector budget, but downstream still paying for all tokens would save no compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eccf1fd02dc72752">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-vcola-a4fb5eab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65f29f75fc6da94d">Why need visual compression for hybrid linear-attention VLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Many vision tokens consume language-layer compute and state, but linear attention stores evidence differently from softmax. V-CoLA uses actual recurrence to select what to merge or skip at deeper layers. Token count alone does not establish answer quality or inference savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compress redundant high-resolution background patches while preserving a small sign the question needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65f29f75fc6da94d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92ed529fc5dae5c4">Why can&#x27;t visual compression for Gated DeltaNet reuse softmax attention weights directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Linear recurrence does not expose the same full attention matrix. State updates and forgetting determine what survives. V-CoLA measures final-state readback for long-term retention and short-window response change for uniqueness, then merges contiguous blocks. These are not ordinary similarity scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An initially salient patch may be overwritten and score poorly on final readback even if local similarity was high.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92ed529fc5dae5c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e0889ed1df84227">What different omissions do long-term retention and short-term uniqueness address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-term readback asks whether a token&#x27;s value remains in final state. Short-term response change asks whether its update adds distinct information. Combine them 0.9/0.1 before contiguous block merging rather than deleting by static similarity alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One token may remain useful long term while another contributes a short-lived detail; neither signal alone captures both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e0889ed1df84227">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc06a879fde2db3d">Why document the transposed state and query probe choices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper uses value×key while the official backend and local code use key×value, requiring transposed recurrence operations. Equation 7 uses a query probe and the appendix shifted keys; local chooses the former and gates on actual state replay with the official kernel. Equivalence is not assumed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversed axes can yield legal shapes but wrong reads, so numerical replay catches errors shape checks miss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现选择, 本地复现, 复现边界与 Evolve. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc06a879fde2db3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:veto" data-paper-title="VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-veto-75da8cb3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-893d97b86bd46781">Why are there both intra-frame and cross-frame redundancies in video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aveto">VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nearby patches can depict one background, and adjacent frames can repeat one scene. VETO removes duplication along space and time. Each compression axis risks losing different details, so total rate alone does not show required motion or local cues survived.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wall repeats within and across frames, but a fleeting hand movement needs both temporal coverage and spatial detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01785">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01785-veto/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-893d97b86bd46781">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:veto" data-paper-title="VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffd7d671be8de7d4">Why merge within frames before removing cross-frame redundancy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aveto">VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intra-frame merging shrinks per-frame candidates, lowering temporal matching cost. Matching all raw patches first already pays that search cost and can yield different correspondences. The order is part of the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compress 100 patches per frame to 20 before matching adjacent frames; the reverse does not save the same work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01785">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01785-veto/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffd7d671be8de7d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:veto" data-paper-title="VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-29587d13df18756f">At fixed token budget, what do more frames versus more positions per frame preserve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aveto">VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More frames favor temporal coverage; more positions favor spatial detail. The local tensor is frames × positions × dimensions, with each keep count bounded by its source axis and output position count equal to their product. No allocation is universally proven optimal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four frames × 16 positions and 16 frames × four both use 64 tokens; the former sees more detail, the latter may catch brief events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01785">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01785-veto/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29587d13df18756f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:veto" data-paper-title="VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-45257d5781bda87f">What does the local farthest-point representative test preserve, and what does it omit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aveto">VETO: Video Efficient Token Optimization for Vision Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deterministic farthest-point representatives test the space-first, time-second sequence and budget, and execute compression on GPU. There is no paper 7B VLM or real video benchmark. The heuristic does not reproduce semantic merging, and author throughput is not a local result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Meeting the token cap confirms both stages ran, not that small-object movement remains recognizable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01785">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01785-veto/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45257d5781bda87f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:video-encoder-selection" data-paper-title="Video Encoders Built on Image Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-video-encoder-selection-2d465377" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-79eabead0b3ea73d">Why select evidence from independently encoded frames before passing them to a language model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avideo-encoder-selection">Video Encoders Built on Image Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Framewise encoding preserves localizable evidence but produces a large sequence for long videos. Selection balances question needs, intra-frame diversity, and cross-frame links under a budget. It does not create evidence; high motion alone need not help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question about which object was picked up first needs that object and cross-frame relations, not every changing background patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06616">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.06616-video-encoder-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79eabead0b3ea73d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:video-encoder-selection" data-paper-title="Video Encoders Built on Image Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a106f0ffb777141">Why refine only retained anchors without adding visual tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avideo-encoder-selection">Video Encoders Built on Image Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection first preserves addressable evidence under a fixed budget. The refiner reads neighboring frames to enrich those anchors without increasing output length. Appending neighbor tokens would break the budget and confound selection with context enrichment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten retained patches can read neighboring motion and still output ten vectors, not ten plus 20 appended positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06616">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.06616-video-encoder-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a106f0ffb777141">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:video-encoder-selection" data-paper-title="Video Encoders Built on Image Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6879eb4eb04dbefb">What do intra-frame DPP and adjacent-frame correspondence rewards constrain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avideo-encoder-selection">Video Encoders Built on Image Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The log-determinant balances quality and diversity to avoid near-duplicate tokens within frames. Cross-frame edges reward matched endpoints that preserve traceable relations. Similarity, margin, and spatial gates apply; edges are not guaranteed true trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select a cup and hand rather than two table patches; keep the cup&#x27;s reliable match in the next frame to see movement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06616">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.06616-video-encoder-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6879eb4eb04dbefb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:video-encoder-selection" data-paper-title="Video Encoders Built on Image Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-378b6dec7ef4d3ae">How are tied pairs and singletons resolved, and why can the selector fill an odd budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avideo-encoder-selection">Video Encoders Built on Image Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Add a pair only if its per-token gain is strictly higher, otherwise add a singleton. Respect quotas and remaining budget. Even with negative gains or no temporal edge, select exactly B distinct indices. Local external uniform quotas and scene proxies are explicit deviations; SITE is not implemented.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One remaining slot permits only a singleton; an equal per-token gain also selects the singleton.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 本地结果与验收边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06616">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.06616-video-encoder-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-378b6dec7ef4d3ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-videomm-bc3e057a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-581d21dad7641725">Why preview video coarsely before spending high-resolution budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-fidelity long-video input is costly, and relevance varies across segments and regions. A Macro Proxy supplies location cues, then detail is requested when coarse evidence is insufficient. Localization and answer evidence are not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Locate a person entering a room, then inspect their hand rather than allocating HD tokens to every segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-581d21dad7641725">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-db0d078e8b45aa47">Why conditionally activate Micro Tokens after a Macro Proxy locates a region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coarse evidence cheaply removes irrelevant areas but can miss tiny text or movements. Activating detail only when needed focuses compute on uncertainty. This preserves coarse-to-fine evidence access rather than enforcing one low-resolution summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing someone hold up a sign may suffice for a yes/no question, but the number on it can require high-resolution tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db0d078e8b45aa47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-25f7d8e5c3ad0407">What is the trade-off between consensus-triggered Micro and equal resolution budgets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed budgets may spend on simple regions; insufficient-consensus activation focuses compute but can miss details if routing fails. Compare identical videos, questions, and cost before claiming better QA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Broad scene-type questions may not need detail; distinguishing similar tools can need it even when macro evidence seems consistent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25f7d8e5c3ad0407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9eec1fc577aafde">Does the macro/micro GPU receipt validate the complete video MLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A100 executed specific state transitions, not a full video MLLM. Trigger counts, selected indices, and budgets are mechanism evidence, not LongVideoBench, throughput, or verification of semantic consensus.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying artificial low consensus and reaching Micro verifies branch execution, not estimating consensus from actual footage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9eec1fc577aafde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-vimod-74b5d3f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d872360a8c146634">Why recover original detail after ViMoD compresses the image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A need for small text or local evidence may emerge mid-generation. ViMoD keeps a compact overview and a recoverable detail cache, and text state selects what to read. This is neither permanent lossy compression nor reading every detail on every step; retrieval has its own costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recognize a receipt first, then recover the tax field when needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d872360a8c146634">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc110d35d7abbcbf">Why does TRACE UPDATE replace the active Fine set rather than accumulate it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulation would let active context grow beyond budget. ViMoD retains Coarse while current generation history decides whether to keep or replace Fine. This changes the attention working set, not permanent storage of recoverable Fine details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replace the left-label working set with a right gauge while keeping the overview and ability to retrieve the label later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc110d35d7abbcbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5803f7913a539b">How do DART&#x27;s learned capacities differ from fixed-size pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed pooling assigns equal position counts to all regions. DART learns region sizes and memberships under a total-capacity constraint, using continuous capacities during training. It adapts granularity but remains budgeted and cannot guarantee every detail survives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group a large blank area together and keep more groups for dense text; a fixed grid cannot adapt that way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5803f7913a539b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-85c9904410c3762f">How do gradients cross DART groups when forward assignments are hard?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Constrained capacities backpropagate through an implicit Jacobian. A hard+soft−stopgrad(soft) estimator uses hard assignments forward and Sinkhorn continuous capacities backward. Stage training needs real Fine-index labels or an online teacher and must fail if missing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A patch is assigned to group A in forward, but continuous assignments can adjust capacity backward. A hardcoded answer region is not learned retrieval evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85c9904410c3762f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

When visual input is too long, which details can be skipped for now, and which need a way to be recovered?

## Takeaway

StackTok optimizes question relevance under a coverage constraint that changes with budget, switching criteria according to the current shortfall. ViMoD's DART builds persistent coarse representations and keeps mappings to original Fine tokens; TRACE uses the generated prefix to keep or replace active details. The former mainly selects a subset before decoding; the latter supports revisiting evidence as needs change during inference.

## Example

Listing all objects requires broad image coverage. Comparing a product label afterward requires local detail. If compression permanently deletes label tokens, later reasoning cannot recover them. Recoverable designs can fetch details but must account for Fine KV storage and retrieval. Long video has a similar trade-off between key frames and temporal coverage.

## Common pitfall

Fewer visual tokens do not imply a proportional drop in whole-system memory or latency. Account for the visual encoder, text decoding, cache, and routing. Recoverability is not free. The local StackTok is a reference selector, while ViMoD has real-checkpoint execution and gradient verification. Neither reproduces the paper's capability gains.

## Reading order

Start with StackTok's relevance/coverage switching for one-time budget allocation. Then compare ViMoD's Coarse/Fine and HOLD/UPDATE decisions to see why multistep reasoning may need fresh evidence. Choose additional frame selection, width pruning, or visual caching papers according to the bottleneck.

1. [StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection](../../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841)
2. [Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning](../../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060)

## Check your understanding

If Fine KV is recoverable, can total visual storage count only the Coarse tokens?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Coarse is the resident active context; Fine KV and its mapping still require storage. Dynamic recovery also consumes bandwidth and routing compute. Report active attention budget, total cache storage, and end-to-end latency separately.

</details>
